answer: Each identity posts staking collateral c, binding a dynamic opportunity-cost bond B=λc and a zero-knowledge verifiable-delay proof that any duplicate key is computationally isolated. Sybil multiplication activates subgame-perfect punishment matrices: slashing penalties α>λ are levied per forged identity, pushing the attack nadir below the gale of honest reward. Ferrous collateral then yields expected attack utility π_B(θ_B−α)+π_G(θ_G−B)<0 for all multipliers. Hence no identity can profitably fork, and honest staking is the strict Nash equilibrium.
